text.p: Non-operating income boosted the earnings of Indonesia's largest automotive firm Astra International for the first nine months of this year, analysts said after a meeting with the company on Wednesday.
Previously analysts had said they were surprised at higher than expected nine-month results, but they had not made any recommendations on the company while awaiting further details.
"Today we found out the details on how the company reached that figure. It mostly came from extraordinary non-operating income," one analyst told Reuters.

He said the company had said it had booked about 42 billion rupiah in extraordinary income in the third quarter, including the sale of land, the sale of a small stake in a telecommunications unit and foreign exhange gains.
Analysts said there had been no significant movement from operating income.
On November 7, the company said it posted operating income of 828.75 billion rupiah in the first nine months of 1996 against 856.56 billion rupiah in the same period last year.
On October 22, Astra announced a net profit of 340.85 billion rupiah in the first nine months of 1996, compared with 271.41 billion rupiah in the year-ago period.
At that time, Astra also said it was raising its forecast for 1996 net profit to 450 billion rupiah, rising to 614 billion rupiah in 1997. ($=2,335 rupiah)
